obstacles: PBDB JSON responses embed an elapsed_time field, so the recorded SHA-256 values cannot be reproduced; counts were compared instead.
PBDB counts are live and drift as records are added or re-identified; no snapshot identifier exists for a count query.

Homonym/mismatch: 'Pieris' resolves in PBDB to Pieris (txn:135135, phylum Angiospermae), not to the record's taxon Pieris (record taxon Pieris (phylum Arthropoda, class Insecta) vs database taxon Pieris (phylum Angiospermae, class Dicotyledoneae)).

'Cephalotes' is a homonym in PBDB (2 taxa share the name); the query resolved to txn:226352 (phylum Arthropoda), consistent with the record's taxon. The base_name count (47) equals the sum of the homonyms' occurrence counts (0 + 47), i.e. it includes every taxon with this name.

'Troglodytes' is a homonym in PBDB (2 taxa share the name); the query resolved to txn:347894 (phylum Chordata), consistent with the record's taxon. The base_name count (5) equals the sum of the homonyms' occurrence counts (0 + 5), i.e. it includes every taxon with this name.

The record's taxon key gbif:1920481 is a different organism with the same name as the PBDB taxon actually counted; the dataset describes the PBDB taxon, so the taxon link (not the count) needs repair.
rationale: Re-fetched 46 of 46 recorded PBDB distribution(s) (pbdb-occs-list) on 2026-10-31; 46 of 46 recorded counts match the live value within tolerance. 46 of 46 queried name(s)/id(s) resolve in PBDB, 45 verifiably to the record's taxon (name or phylum/class agree); 1 resolve to a different organism (Pieris -> Pieris). PBDB checksums are unreproducible by construction (elapsed_time in every response), but recorded byte sizes are consistent with the live responses. The identifier resolves. Source authority, independence and authenticity are inherited from sources/paleobiology-database.json with the per-record caps noted.
